gloss: home run; big hit; major success

definitions.explanation: A hit in baseball that allows the batter to round all bases and score. One of the most exciting plays in baseball.
Used figuratively to describe a spectacular success or achievement, similar to English 'hitting it out of the park.'

examples.japanese: ホームランを{打|う}った。
{満塁|まんるい}ホームランで{逆転|ぎゃくてん}した。
examples.english: They came from behind with a grand slam.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{今季|こんき}{三十本|さんじゅっぽん}のホームランを{打|う}って{本塁打王|ほんるいだおう}に{輝|かがや}いた。
examples.english: He hit thirty home runs this season and was crowned home run champion.

examples.japanese: あの{企画|きかく}はホームランだった。
examples.english: That project was a home run.

examples.japanese: {今回|こんかい}の{新商品|しんしょうひん}はホームラン{級|きゅう}のヒットだ。
examples.english: This new product is a blockbuster hit.

examples.japanese: ヒットを{積|つ}み{重|かさ}ねるよりも、{一発|いっぱつ}ホームランを{狙|ねら}うタイプの{経営者|けいえいしゃ}だ。
examples.english: He's the type of businessman who goes for the big win rather than building up small successes.

notes:
A loanword from English, deeply embedded in Japanese culture due to the enormous popularity of baseball in Japan. Also written as {本塁打|ほんるいだ} in formal sports writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ホームランを{打|う}つ: to hit a home run
- {満塁|まんるい}ホームラン: grand slam
- {逆転|ぎゃくてん}ホームラン: come-from-behind home run
- ホームラン{級|きゅう}: home-run-level (spectacular)
- {本塁打|ほんるいだ}{王|おう}: home run champion

CULTURAL NOTE:
Baseball ({野球|やきゅう}) is Japan's most popular spectator sport. Home run records and home run derbies receive extensive media coverage. The figurative use of ホームラン is very common in business and everyday conversation to describe any outstanding success.
